s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive visual impairment with night blindness and scotomas
salient_findings: Night blindness since childhood
Inferonasal scotoma on Goldmann visual field
Abnormal electroretinogram with flat rod response
Hypofluorescence on fundus autofluorescence
Inner retinal thickening and disorganization on OCT
key_facts: Patient age 42
Symptoms present since childhood
No symptoms except night blindness
Visual acuity 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes
Color vision normal
Few yellow spots on fundus examination
Indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades
Inferonasal scotoma on Goldmann visual field
Electroretinogram shows large, slow scotopic and photopic responses
Flat rod electroretinogram
Lower ERG amplitudes compared to 30 years ago
Fundus autofluorescence shows hypofluorescence in superotemporal zones
Narrow hyperfluorescent ring inside on fundus autofluorescence
Central macula appears unremarkable on fundus autofluorescence
OCT shows supernormal thickness in perifoveal region
OCT shows marked inner retinal thickening and disorganization in eccentric areas
Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in superotemporal region on OCT

shortlist.label: Rod-cone dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive visual impairment, night blindness, and flat rod electroretinogram

raw.rationale: The patient's night blindness since childhood, normal color vision, and specific findings on electroretinogram (large, slow scotopic and photopic responses with a flat rod electroretinogram) along with the progressive nature of the condition (lower ERG amplitudes compared to 30 years ago) are consistent with rod-cone dystrophy. The presence of few yellow spots on fundus examination, inferonasal scotoma, and specific OCT findings (supernormal thickness in perifoveal region, marked inner retinal thickening and disorganization in eccentric areas, and complete loss of photoreceptors in superotemporal region) also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Retinitis pigmentosa
rejected.why: While retinitis pigmentosa could explain night blindness, the absence of pigmentary degeneration on fundus examination and the specific pattern of retinal changes on OCT and fundus autofluorescence do not fully align with typical retinitis pigmentosa findings.

rejected.label: Choroideremia
rejected.why: Choroideremia typically presents with more significant choroidal and retinal atrophy and often affects central vision earlier, which does not match the patient's preserved visual acuity and specific pattern of retinal changes.

rejected.label: Gyrate atrophy
rejected.why: Gyrate atrophy is characterized by well-defined areas of chorioretinal atrophy that progress over time, which is not the primary finding in this patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Leber congenital amaurosis
rejected.why: Leber congenital amaurosis typically presents with severe visual impairment from birth, which does not align with this patient's relatively preserved visual acuity and later presentation of symptoms.
